thread:
Samir: FYI — noticed sustained egress throttle errors from eu-west1 this morning around 09:12 UTC. A subset of background embedding batches and async exports are failing. I want to propose a short targeted maintenance window to reprovision NATs and rotate routing rules. Need to coordinate oncall handoff, statuspage copy, and a customer-facing blurb.

Oncall Bot: :rotating_light: INCIDENT DETECTED (network-egress-eu-west1) — alert group: infra-network — priority: P2 — paging Samir.

Maya: looking at logs now. Confirming higher 5xx rates from embedding-runner nodes calling out to third-party storage via the NATs. Latency spikes ~ 10s for TCP handshake + TLS.

Jordan (sre-lead): @Samir thanks — do we have blast radius? which customers or routes are impacted?

Samir: Primarily internal batch jobs and non-SLA async exports; real-time hosted API traffic (user-facing generation) seems fine due to egress route pinned to different subnets. I estimate impact to "bulk embeddings" customers and ingestion pipelines for some enterprise customers. No evidence of data loss.

Priya (ops): propose a 20-minute targeted drain for the affected worker pool, then rotate NAT gateways. Can we schedule immediately as an emergency maintenance?

Lena (product-comms): if we go ahead, I'll prepare a concise statuspage + customer email. Draft below — please edit.

Lena (product-comms): [statuspage draft]

```
Status: Investigating — Partial service disruption (eu-west1)
Impact: Background batch jobs and async exports may fail or be delayed. Real-time API unaffected.
Start time: 2026-03-15 09:12 UTC
Next update: in 15 minutes or at milestone
Mitigation: targeted worker drain and NAT rotation in progress
```

Samir: +1 on that copy. Suggest adding: "No action required by customers; jobs will be retried automatically."

Maya: I'm running live tcpdump on one of the affected nodes, will paste a short snippet:

```
14:15:22.123456 IP hostA.443 > nat-gw: Flags [S], seq 0, win 64240, options [mss 1460,sackOK,TS val 123456 ecr 0], length 0
14:15:22.223456 IP nat-gw > hostA.443: Flags [RST], seq 0, win 0, length 0
```

Jordan (sre-lead): RSTs from the NAT indicate we should rotate gateway. Priya — initiate drain playbook and place a short maintenance marker on infra. I'll own escalations.

Priya (ops): Kicking off drain now. Commands: 

```
# drain pool
rwctl pool drain --pool embeddings-euw1 --grace 60
# rotate nat
infractl nat rotate --region eu-west1 --group batch-nat
```

Samir: Oncall handoff: I'm going offline for a partial system restart at +5. @Jordan you're primary until I confirm completion. If issues escalate, page SRE on-call.

Oncall Bot: @Jordan (sre-lead) acknowledged the page. Bridge created: https://meet.redwood/bridge/1768409999

Maya: drain progressing, jobs are being rescheduled to other pools. Upload failures dropping from ~50/min to ~5/min.

Lena (product-comms): customer email (short) draft: 

```
Subject: Brief disruption to background exports in eu-west1 — we're on it
Hi — we detected an issue impacting background exports in eu-west1. We've initiated a short maintenance to rotate network gateways; most realtime API traffic is unaffected. No customer action required — jobs will be retried automatically. We'll update you when the maintenance completes. — Redwood Inference
```

Samir: Good. Jordan — once NAT rotation finishes, do a quick smoke: trigger a test batch and confirm exports succeed.

Jordan (sre-lead): NAT rotation completed at 09:23 UTC. Running smoke.

Maya: smoke test results: 10/10 test exports succeeded, latency normalized to baseline.

Oncall Bot: STATUS CHANGE — incident network-egress-eu-west1: Mitigated.

Samir: Closing the bridge. I'll post the final statuspage and send the customer email. Final internal notes: cause likely transient provider-side NAT instability; mitigated by rotating NAT and draining batch pool. Action item: schedule a postmortem with provider and add NAT health probes to our telemetry.

Lena (product-comms): Posted status update and sent customer email at 09:32 UTC. Copy below for records.

```
Update: 09:32 UTC — Mitigation complete. Background exports resume; no further action required.
```

Priya (ops): marking incident as resolved in the ops tracker. Assigning follow-ups: provider postmortem to Samir, telemetry task to Maya.

Samir: Thanks everyone. Quick retrospective note: consider a small prewarmed spare NAT group to avoid rotational delays for batch workloads.

Jordan (sre-lead): Agreed. I'll capture in the postmortem ticket. :white_check_mark:
